source.text: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.

records.literal_gloss: On the but first of the week, at dawn deep, to the tomb they came bringing which they had prepared spices.

en.L: But on the first [day] of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared.
en.B: Very early on the first day of the week, at the first light of dawn, the women came to the tomb. They brought with them the spices they had made ready.
en.R: On Sunday morning, very early, the women went to the tomb. They took with them the sweet-smelling spices they had made.

fr.L: Mais le premier [jour] de la semaine, très tôt à l’aube, elles vinrent au tombeau, apportant les aromates qu’elles avaient préparés.
fr.B: Le premier jour de la semaine, de très bonne heure, aux premières lueurs de l’aube, les femmes se rendirent au tombeau. Elles apportaient les aromates qu’elles avaient préparés.
fr.R: Le dimanche, très tôt le matin, les femmes sont allées au tombeau. Elles ont emporté les épices parfumées qu’elles avaient préparées.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: the day after the Sabbath, our Sunday
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "the first of the Sabbaths"; the plural is used for the week, counted from one Sabbath to the next. The women had rested on the Sabbath, as the law required (23:56), and came as soon as it was over.

decisions.choice: at early dawn: in the first light of morning
decisions.reason: The words are "deep dawn", the earliest part of the morning, when the light is just beginning.

decisions.choice: the spices they had prepared: sweet-smelling oils and spices for the body
decisions.reason: The women had prepared them on Friday evening before the Sabbath began (23:56). They were put on a body in its wrappings as a last act of love and honor; there had been no time to do it when Jesus was buried (23:53-54).

decisions.choice: they: the women from Galilee of 23:55
decisions.reason: The verb continues the account from 23:55-56; the women are named in 24:10.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since a new chapter begins here.

decisions.choice: On Sunday morning
alternatives: On the first day of the week
decisions.reason: Readable names the day in the way readers count the week today.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("il voit", 24:12)
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Luke, John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, including the travellers' account in 24:19-24. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα.

records.literal_gloss: They found then the stone having been rolled away from the tomb, \v 3 having entered however not they found the body.

en.L: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb, \v 3 but having gone in, they did not find the body.
en.B: They found that the stone had been rolled back from the tomb. \v 3 But when they went inside, they found no body there.
en.R: When they got there, they saw that the large stone in front of the tomb had been rolled away. \v 3 They went inside, but the body was not there.

fr.L: Et elles trouvèrent la pierre roulée hors du tombeau, \v 3 mais, étant entrées, elles ne trouvèrent pas le corps.
fr.B: Elles trouvèrent la pierre roulée à l’écart du tombeau. \v 3 Mais, une fois entrées, elles n’y trouvèrent pas le corps.
fr.R: Quand elles sont arrivées, elles ont vu que la grosse pierre placée devant le tombeau avait été roulée sur le côté. \v 3 Elles sont entrées, mais le corps n’était pas là.

decisions.choice: the stone: the large stone that closed the entrance of a tomb cut in rock
decisions.reason: Tombs of the time were cut into rock, and a heavy stone, often shaped like a disk, was rolled across the doorway (Mark 15:46). Luke does not say who rolled it away.

decisions.choice: the body: the reading of the SBLGNT, with no name added
alternatives: the body of the Lord Jesus, the reading of most manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 and Codex Vaticanus among them, read "the body of the Lord Jesus". Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts have only "the body", and the SBLGNT follows them here. The title "the Lord Jesus" is common in Acts but is found nowhere else in Luke's Gospel, which is one reason some think it was added. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the large stone in front of the tomb
decisions.reason: Readable says what the stone was there for, since Luke has not mentioned it before.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the being perplexed them about this and behold men two stood by them in clothing flashing like lightning.

en.L: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that, look, two men stood by them in clothing flashing like lightning.
en.B: They were at a loss to know what this meant. Then two men were standing by them, their clothing flashing with light.
en.R: The women did not know what to think. Suddenly two men were standing beside them. Their clothes were as bright as lightning.

fr.L: Et il arriva, tandis qu’elles étaient perplexes à ce sujet, que voici, deux hommes se tinrent près d’elles, dans un vêtement qui étincelait comme l’éclair.
fr.B: Elles ne savaient qu’en penser. C’est alors que deux hommes se tinrent près d’elles, en vêtements éclatants de lumière.
fr.R: Les femmes ne savaient pas quoi penser. Tout à coup, deux hommes se sont trouvés à côté d’elles. Leurs vêtements brillaient comme l’éclair.

decisions.choice: perplexed: at a loss, unable to explain it
decisions.reason: The verb describes someone who can find no way through a problem. Fear comes in the next verse.

decisions.choice: two men: angels, who look like men
decisions.reason: Luke calls them men, as they appeared, but the two from Emmaus later call this "a vision of angels" (24:23). Two men in shining clothing also appear at the ascension (Acts 1:10), and Moses and Elijah stood with Jesus in glory (9:30-32).

decisions.choice: flashing like lightning: shining with a light that is not of this world
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for lightning (17:24). Jesus' clothing was "white and flashing" at the transfiguration (9:29).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to the sudden appearance. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: Suddenly
decisions.reason: Readable carries the force of "look" and the old storytelling formula with one word.

source.text: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Terrified then having become them and bowing the faces to the ground they said to them, Why seek you the living [one] among the dead?

en.L: And as they became terrified and bowed [their] faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
en.B: The women were terrified and kept their faces bowed to the ground. But the men said to them, "Why are you looking among the dead for the one who is alive?
en.R: The women were very frightened and bowed down with their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why are you looking for someone who is alive in a place for dead people?

fr.L: Et comme elles étaient saisies de crainte et inclinaient le visage vers la terre, ils leur dirent : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous le vivant parmi les morts ?
fr.B: Les femmes, effrayées, gardaient le visage incliné vers le sol. Mais les hommes leur dirent : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous parmi les morts celui qui est vivant ?
fr.R: Les femmes ont eu très peur et se sont inclinées, le visage contre le sol. Les hommes leur ont dit : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous chez les morts quelqu’un qui est vivant ?

decisions.choice: bowing their faces to the ground: a sign of fear and respect before a heavenly being
decisions.reason: People bow low when they meet a messenger from God (Daniel 8:17). The women cannot look at the men.

decisions.choice: the living one: one person who is alive, Jesus
alternatives: the living, meaning living people in general
decisions.reason: The word is singular and masculine, "the one who lives". The question is about Jesus, who is alive; the tomb is a place for the dead.

decisions.choice: Why do you seek the living one among the dead: a gentle rebuke
decisions.reason: The question says that the women are looking in the wrong place. In Acts Jesus is "the Author of life" (Acts 3:15), and "the living one" echoes how Scripture speaks of the living God.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who spoke, since the women are the subject of the first half of the sentence.

source.text: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη.

records.literal_gloss: Not he is here, but he has been raised.

en.L: He is not here, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been raised.
en.B: He is not here; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been raised.
en.R: He is not here. He has been raised to life!

fr.L: Il n’est pas ici, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été ressuscité.
fr.B: Il n’est pas ici ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été ressuscité.
fr.R: Il n’est pas ici. Il a été ramené à la vie !

decisions.choice: the sentence is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sentence is left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have these words. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack them. Some think they were added from Mark 16:6 or Matthew 28:6, but the wording here is not quite the same as either. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he has been raised: God has raised him
alternatives: he has risen by his own power
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, the form Luke uses for God's act of raising Jesus (9:22; 24:34; Acts 3:15). Jesus also speaks of himself as rising (18:33; 24:7, 46); both are true.

decisions.choice: raised to life
decisions.reason: Readable says what "raised" means here.

source.text: μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, λέγων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Remember how he spoke to you yet being in the Galilee, \v 7 saying the Son of Man that it is necessary to be delivered into hands of men sinful and to be crucified and the third day to rise.

en.L: Remember how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still in Galilee, \v 7 saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into [the] hands of sinful {{gender:people|men}} and be crucified and on the third day rise."
en.B: Remember what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still in Galilee. \v 7 He said that the Son of Man had to be handed over to sinful {{gender:people|men}} and be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
en.R: Remember what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you back in Galilee. \v 7 He said, 'The Son of Man must be handed over to sinful {{gender:people|men}}. They will nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise from death.'"

fr.L: Souvenez-vous comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a parlé quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore en Galilée, \v 7 en disant que le Fils de l’homme doit être livré entre les mains d’{{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs, et être crucifié, et, le troisième jour, ressusciter. »
fr.B: Rappelez-vous ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a dit quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore en Galilée. \v 7 Il a dit que le Fils de l’homme devait être livré à des {{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs et être crucifié, et que le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressusciterait. »
fr.R: Rappelez-vous ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a dit quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était là-bas, en Galilée. \v 7 Il a dit : “Le Fils de l’homme doit être livré à des {{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs. Ils vont {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix. Mais le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va revenir à la vie.” »

decisions.choice: how he spoke to you in Galilee: Jesus' warnings about his death and rising
decisions.reason: Jesus told his disciples while still in Galilee that the Son of Man would suffer, be killed and be raised on the third day (9:22, 9:44), and said it again on the way to Jerusalem (18:31-33). The women from Galilee were among his followers (8:1-3; 23:55), so they too had heard it.

decisions.choice: must: what had to happen by God's purpose
decisions.reason: The word is the one Jesus used in 9:22 and uses again in 24:26 and 24:44: the suffering and rising are what God planned and the Scriptures foretold.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 9:22, the title is Jesus' way of speaking about himself and his mission.

decisions.choice: sinful people: those who do not follow God's law
decisions.reason: The phrase may point to the Gentiles who carried out the execution, but it covers all who handed Jesus over and put him to death (18:32; 24:20).

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, so it follows the gender setting, as 9:44 does.

decisions.choice: Jesus' words quoted directly
decisions.reason: Readable turns the reported words into a quotation, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: They will nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains what crucifixion was.

source.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they remembered the words of him, \v 9 and having returned from the tomb they told these things all to the eleven and to all the rest.

en.L: And they remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words, \v 9 and having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words came back to them. \v 9 They went back from the tomb and reported all of this to the Eleven and to everyone else.
en.R: Then the women remembered what Jesus had said. \v 9 They left the tomb and went back to the city. They told the eleven apostles and all the other followers of Jesus about everything that had happened.

fr.L: Et elles se souvinrent de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles, \v 9 et, revenues du tombeau, elles rapportèrent toutes ces choses aux onze et à tous les autres.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles leur revinrent en mémoire. \v 9 Elles quittèrent le tombeau et allèrent annoncer tout cela aux Onze et à tous les autres.
fr.R: Alors les femmes se sont souvenues de ce que Jésus avait dit. \v 9 Elles ont quitté le tombeau et sont retournées en ville. Elles ont raconté tout ce qui s’était passé aux onze apôtres et à tous les autres qui suivaient Jésus.

decisions.choice: remembered his words: now understood what he had said
decisions.reason: The disciples had not understood the warnings when they first heard them (9:45; 18:34). Now the women remember them and see what they meant.

decisions.choice: the eleven: the Twelve without Judas
decisions.reason: Judas had betrayed Jesus (22:3-6, 47-48), so the apostles were now eleven. Luke tells of the choice of a twelfth in Acts 1:15-26.

decisions.choice: all the rest: the wider group of disciples
decisions.reason: Other followers were with the apostles, among them the two who set out for Emmaus (24:13, 33).

decisions.choice: went back to the city
decisions.reason: Readable says where they went; the apostles were in Jerusalem (24:33).

decisions.choice: the Eleven (B); the eleven apostles (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced capitalizes the group's name, as with "the Twelve" (9:1); Readable says who they were.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: Were now the Magdalene Mary and Joanna and Mary the [mother] of James and the rest with them; they were telling to the apostles these things.

en.L: Now they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the [mother] of James, and the rest [of the women] with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.
en.B: The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the others who were with them. They kept telling the apostles about these things.
en.R: The women who told the apostles these things were Mary from the town of Magdala, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and some other women who were with them.

fr.L: Or c’étaient Marie la Magdaléenne, et Jeanne, et Marie, [la mère] de Jacques, et les autres [femmes] avec elles ; elles disaient ces choses aux apôtres.
fr.B: C’étaient Marie de Magdala, Jeanne, Marie, mère de Jacques, et les autres femmes qui étaient avec elles. Elles ne cessaient de raconter cela aux apôtres.
fr.R: Les femmes qui ont raconté tout cela aux apôtres étaient Marie, de la ville de Magdala, Jeanne, Marie, la mère de Jacques, et d’autres femmes qui étaient avec elles.

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene and Joanna: women who had followed Jesus from Galilee
decisions.reason: Luke has named them before: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out, and Joanna the wife of Chuza, a manager in Herod's household (8:2-3). They provided for Jesus and the Twelve from their own means.

decisions.choice: Mary the mother of James
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of James", a common way of naming a woman by a family member. Mark 15:40 and 16:1 call her the mother of James, so "mother" is supplied.

decisions.choice: were telling: told again and again
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect tense: the women kept telling the apostles, who would not believe them (24:11).

decisions.choice: the women are the first witnesses
alternatives: the apostles are the first witnesses
decisions.reason: Luke names the women as the first to hear that Jesus had been raised and the first to tell it, though the testimony of women was often given little weight at the time.

decisions.choice: one sentence that names the women who told the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable joins the list and the telling, which is how the two clauses relate.

decisions.choice: Mary from the town of Magdala
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name: Magdala was a town on the Lake of Galilee, as at 8:2.

source.text: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And appeared before them like nonsense the words these, and they were disbelieving them.

en.L: And these words appeared before them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
en.B: But to the apostles the report sounded like nonsense, and they would not believe the women.
en.R: But the apostles thought the women's story was foolish talk. They would not believe them.

fr.L: Et ces paroles parurent à leurs yeux comme du délire, et ils ne les croyaient pas.
fr.B: Mais ce récit parut aux apôtres n’être que du délire, et ils refusaient de croire les femmes.
fr.R: Mais les apôtres ont pensé que l’histoire des femmes était absurde. Ils refusaient de les croire.

decisions.choice: nonsense: idle talk, wild stories
decisions.reason: The word is used for empty chatter or the talk of someone who is not in their right mind. The apostles do not think the women are lying, only that their story cannot be true.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: they went on refusing to believe
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes continuing unbelief. The theme of slowness to believe runs through the chapter (24:25, 38, 41).

decisions.choice: the apostles ... the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant by each "them".

decisions.choice: du délire (L, B); absurde (R)
decisions.reason: The word is idle or wild talk (m1). "Sornettes" and "balivernes" sound quaint, and "radotage" suggests an old person repeating himself; "du délire" is the current word for talk that makes no sense, and it says as strongly as the Greek how the report was received.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.

records.literal_gloss: But Peter having risen up ran to the tomb, and having stooped down he sees the linen cloths alone, and he went away to himself wondering at that having happened.

en.L: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb; and stooping to look in, he sees the linen cloths alone; and he went away to his home, marveling at what had happened.
en.B: Peter, though, got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down to look in and saw nothing but the linen wrappings. Then he went home, amazed at what had taken place.
en.R: But Peter jumped up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and looked inside. All he saw were the strips of linen cloth that had been wrapped around the body. Then he went home, amazed and wondering what had happened.

fr.L: Mais Pierre, s’étant levé, courut au tombeau ; et, se penchant, il voit les linges seuls ; et il s’en alla chez lui, s’étonnant de ce qui était arrivé.
fr.B: Pierre, cependant, se leva et courut au tombeau. Il se pencha pour regarder à l’intérieur et ne vit que les bandes de lin. Puis il rentra chez lui, étonné de ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Mais Pierre s’est levé d’un bond et a couru au tombeau. Il s’est penché et a regardé à l’intérieur. Il a vu seulement les bandes de tissu qu’on avait enroulées autour du corps. Puis il est rentré chez lui. Il était étonné et se demandait ce qui s’était passé.

decisions.choice: the verse is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have the verse. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack it. Some think it was added from John 20:3-10, which tells of Peter and another disciple at the tomb; but the visit to the tomb is mentioned again in 24:24. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he sees: a vivid present in the middle of a past account
decisions.reason: Luke switches to the present tense to put the reader beside Peter at the moment he looks in.

decisions.choice: the linen cloths alone: the burial wrappings, with no body in them
decisions.reason: The word is for strips or pieces of linen used to wrap a body (John 19:40). That they lay there "alone" shows that the body had not been carried off in its wrappings.

decisions.choice: went away to his home
decisions.reason: The phrase is "to himself". It most likely means to where he was staying (John 20:10 has a similar phrase). Some join it to the next word: "wondering to himself".

decisions.choice: that had been wrapped around the body
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the cloths were.

decisions.choice: saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the past tense of the story.

decisions.choice: les linges (L); les bandes de lin (B); les bandes de tissu qu’on avait enroulées autour du corps (R)
decisions.reason: The word is strips or pieces of linen used to wrap the body (m3). "Bandelettes" makes French readers think of Egyptian mummies; "les linges" is the plain word at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say what the cloths were.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: And behold two of them on same the day were going to a village being distant stadia sixty from Jerusalem, whose name [was] Emmaus, \v 14 and they were talking with one another about all these things having happened.

en.L: And look, on that same day two of them were going to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, whose name [was] Emmaus, \v 14 and they were talking with one another about all these things that had happened.
en.B: On that very day two of them were walking to Emmaus, a village {{units:about seven miles|sixty stadia}} from Jerusalem. \v 14 They were deep in conversation about all that had happened.
en.R: That same day two of Jesus' followers were walking to a village called Emmaus. It was {{units:about seven miles|sixty stadia}} from Jerusalem. \v 14 On the way they talked with each other about all these events.

fr.L: Et voici, ce même jour, deux d’entre eux se rendaient à un village distant de soixante stades de Jérusalem, dont le nom [était] Emmaüs, \v 14 et ils s’entretenaient l’un avec l’autre de toutes ces choses qui étaient arrivées.
fr.B: Ce même jour, deux d’entre eux se rendaient à Emmaüs, un village situé à {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} de Jérusalem. \v 14 Ils discutaient longuement de tout ce qui était arrivé.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, deux disciples de Jésus marchaient vers un village appelé Emmaüs. Il était à {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} de Jérusalem. \v 14 En chemin, ils parlaient ensemble de tout ce qui s’était passé.

decisions.choice: two of them: two of the wider group of disciples, not of the eleven
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to "all the rest" with the eleven (24:9). When the two return, they find "the eleven and those with them" (24:33). One is named Cleopas (24:18).

decisions.choice: sixty stadia: about seven miles (11 kilometers)
decisions.reason: A stadion was a Greek measure of about 607 feet (185 meters). Sixty of them make a walk of two or three hours.

decisions.choice: sixty: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a hundred and sixty, the reading of Codex Sinaiticus and some other manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read sixty. Codex Sinaiticus and a few others read a hundred and sixty, which would fit a town called Emmaus about 19 miles from Jerusalem but would make the return the same evening (24:33) very hard. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Emmaus: a village whose location is no longer certain
decisions.reason: Several places have been suggested. Luke gives only the distance from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to begin a new scene. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: about seven miles as the default, sixty stadia as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the distance in modern measure; the Measures setting shows the original unit. Literal keeps the unit of the Greek.

decisions.choice: Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" refers to.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} (B, R); soixante stades (L)
decisions.reason: French readers measure distance in kilometres, so the default is metric rather than the English miles; sixty stadia were about 11 kilometres (m2). The Measures setting shows the original unit, and Literal keeps it.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the talking them and discussing that himself Jesus having drawn near was walking along with them, \v 16 but the eyes of them were held [so as] not to recognize him.

en.L: And it happened, while they were talking and discussing, that Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} drew near and was walking along with them, \v 16 but their eyes were held back from recognizing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: While they were talking it over and debating, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came near and began to walk with them. \v 16 But their eyes were held back, and they did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: While they were talking and trying to understand it all, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came up and walked along with them. \v 16 But their eyes were kept from knowing who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

fr.L: Et il arriva, tandis qu’ils s’entretenaient et discutaient, que Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, s’étant approché, faisait route avec eux, \v 16 mais leurs yeux étaient empêchés de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnaître.
fr.B: Pendant qu’ils parlaient et discutaient, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} s’approcha et se mit à marcher avec eux. \v 16 Mais leurs yeux étaient comme retenus, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent pas.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils parlaient et essayaient de tout comprendre, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est arrivé près d’eux et a marché avec eux. \v 16 Mais quelque chose empêchait leurs yeux de voir qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était.

decisions.choice: discussing: debating, asking each other questions
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or examine together. They are trying to make sense of what has happened.

decisions.choice: their eyes were held back: they were kept from recognizing him
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who held their eyes. The same eyes are "opened" in 24:31, which suggests that God kept them from knowing him until the right moment. The question is left open, and every level keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself came near: the risen Jesus joins his followers
decisions.reason: "Himself" stresses that it was Jesus, though they did not know it. The reader knows more than the two travelers.

decisions.choice: trying to understand it all
decisions.reason: Readable says what their discussion was about.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες;

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them, What [are] the words these that you are exchanging with one another walking?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What [are] these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk?"
en.B: He said to them, "What is this conversation you are having with each other as you walk?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "What is all this you are saying to each other on the road?"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Quelles [sont] ces paroles que vous échangez l’un avec l’autre en marchant ? »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Quelle est cette conversation que vous avez ensemble en chemin ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « De quoi parlez-vous ensemble sur la route ? »

decisions.choice: exchanging: tossing words back and forth
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw one thing against another. It pictures a lively exchange, each answering the other.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.

records.literal_gloss: And they stood still looking sad.

en.L: And they stood still, looking sad.
en.B: They stopped walking, and their faces were gloomy.
en.R: They stopped, and their faces looked very sad.

fr.L: Et ils s’arrêtèrent, l’air triste.
fr.B: Ils s’arrêtèrent, le visage sombre.
fr.R: Ils se sont arrêtés. Ils avaient l’air très tristes.

decisions.choice: looking sad: gloomy, with sorrow on the face
decisions.reason: The word describes a dark or sad face, as of those who fast to be seen in Matthew 6:16.

decisions.choice: they stood still, looking sad: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the question goes on, "... as you walk and are sad?", the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have a new sentence, "And they stood still, looking sad." Many later ones make the sadness part of Jesus' question. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;

records.literal_gloss: Answering now one named Cleopas said to him, You alone are visiting Jerusalem and not have known the things having happened in it in the days these?

en.L: And one, named Cleopas, answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the only one staying in Jerusalem and [yet] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not known the things that have happened in it in these days?"
en.B: One of them, a man named Cleopas, answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be the one visitor in Jerusalem who has not heard what has gone on there in the past few days?"
en.R: One of them, named Cleopas, answered, "You must be the only person staying in Jerusalem who does not know! Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not heard what has happened there in the last few days?"

fr.L: Et l’un, nommé Cléopas, répondant, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Tu es le seul à séjourner à Jérusalem et [pourtant] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’as pas su ce qui s’y est passé ces jours-ci ? »
fr.B: L’un d’eux, un homme nommé Cléopas, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Serais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le seul visiteur de Jérusalem à ignorer ce qui s’y est passé ces derniers jours ? »
fr.R: L’un d’eux, qui s’appelait Cléopas, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a répondu : « Tu dois être le seul visiteur de Jérusalem qui ne sait pas ! Tu n’as pas entendu ce qui s’est passé là-bas ces derniers jours ? »

decisions.choice: staying in: living as a visitor
decisions.reason: The verb is used for living somewhere as a stranger. Jerusalem was crowded with visitors for the Passover (22:1); Cleopas takes Jesus for one of them.

decisions.choice: Cleopas: a follower of Jesus named only here
decisions.reason: He is not one of the Twelve. He may be the Clopas of John 19:25, but the names are spelled differently and the Gospels do not say.

decisions.choice: a question expressing surprise
decisions.reason: The sentence can be read as a statement, "You alone ... do not know", but the surprise is the same either way: everyone in Jerusalem knows.

decisions.choice: an exclamation followed by a question
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question to bring out Cleopas's surprise.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ποῖα;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, What things?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What things?"
en.B: "What things?" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them.
en.R: Jesus asked, "What things?"

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Quelles choses ? »
fr.B: Il leur demanda : « Quoi donc ? »
fr.R: Jésus a demandé : « Qu’est-ce qui s’est passé ? »

decisions.choice: What things: a question that draws them out
alternatives: a sign that Jesus did not know
decisions.reason: Jesus asks so that they will tell what they think has happened, as he lets them do in the verses that follow.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ, ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people, \v 20 how also delivered up him the chief priests and the rulers of us to [the] judgment of death and crucified him.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "The things about Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people, \v 20 and how the chief priests and our rulers handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to a sentence of death and crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "About Jesus from Nazareth. He was a prophet, a man whose deeds and words had great power in the eyes of God and of all the people. \v 20 And our chief priests and leaders handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to be condemned to death, and they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "About Jesus from the town of Nazareth. He was a prophet. God and all the people could see the power of what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did and said. \v 20 But our chief priests and rulers handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to be sentenced to death. They had {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} nailed to a cross.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Ce qui concerne Jésus le Nazarénien, qui était un homme, un prophète puissant en œuvre et en parole devant Dieu et devant tout le peuple, \v 20 et comment les chefs des prêtres et nos dirigeants {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont livré à une condamnation à mort et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont crucifié.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Ce qui concerne Jésus de Nazareth. C’était un prophète, un homme dont les actes et les paroles avaient une grande puissance aux yeux de Dieu et de tout le peuple. \v 20 Et nos chefs des prêtres et nos dirigeants {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont livré pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit condamné à mort, et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont crucifié.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont répondu : « Ce qui est arrivé à Jésus, de la ville de Nazareth. C’était un prophète. Dieu et tout le peuple pouvaient voir la puissance de ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait et disait. \v 20 Mais nos chefs des prêtres et nos dirigeants {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont livré pour qu’on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} condamne à mort. Ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont fait clouer sur une croix.

decisions.choice: a man, a prophet mighty: a prophet whose power everyone could see
alternatives: a mighty man who was a prophet
decisions.reason: The crowds had called Jesus a great prophet (7:16; 9:19). The two disciples still speak of him that way. "Mighty in deed and word" is how Stephen describes Moses (Acts 7:22).

decisions.choice: before God and all the people: in the sight of God and of everyone
alternatives: in front of God and the people in a court
decisions.reason: God approved of what Jesus did, and the whole nation saw it (Acts 2:22).

decisions.choice: the chief priests and our rulers: the leaders of the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The same leaders handed Jesus over to Pilate (23:1, 13). The rulers are the members of the council (23:35).

decisions.choice: they crucified him: they caused his crucifixion
alternatives: they nailed him to the cross with their own hands
decisions.reason: Roman soldiers carried out the execution (23:33-36), but those who demanded it are said to have done it, as Peter says in Acts 2:23 and 2:36.

decisions.choice: the speech continues past the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT closes the sentence at the end of 24:20, but Cleopas's answer goes on to 24:24.

decisions.choice: the description of Jesus as a sentence of its own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long answer into shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: They had him nailed to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains crucifixion and keeps the leaders responsible without saying they did it with their own hands.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.

records.literal_gloss: We however were hoping that he it is the [one] being about to redeem Israel; but indeed also with all these things third this day it brings since which these things happened.

en.L: But we were hoping that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who is going to redeem Israel; but indeed, besides all these things, it is [the] third day today since these things happened.
en.B: Our hope was that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the one who would redeem Israel. And on top of all that, this is now the third day since it happened.
en.R: We hoped that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the one who would rescue Israel and set our people free. And now it has been three days since all this happened.

fr.L: Mais nous, nous espérions que c’était {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui allait racheter Israël ; mais, en plus de tout cela, c’est aujourd’hui le troisième jour depuis que ces choses sont arrivées.
fr.B: Nous espérions que c’était {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui rachèterait Israël. Et en plus de tout cela, voici déjà le troisième jour depuis que c’est arrivé.
fr.R: Nous espérions que c’était {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui allait délivrer Israël et rendre la liberté à notre peuple. Et maintenant, cela fait trois jours que tout cela est arrivé.

decisions.choice: redeem: set free, as by paying a price
decisions.reason: The verb is used for buying the freedom of a slave or captive. Zechariah praised God for bringing redemption to his people (1:68), and Anna spoke about Jesus to all who waited for the redemption of Jerusalem (2:38). The two disciples hoped that Jesus would free Israel, as God freed the people from Egypt.

decisions.choice: we were hoping: a hope they now think has ended
decisions.reason: The past continuous tense describes a hope that went on until his death. The reader knows that the hope was not wrong, only too small (24:46-47).

decisions.choice: it is the third day: this day makes three since it happened
decisions.reason: The words are "it brings this third day". Counting the day of the crucifixion as the first, Sunday is the third. Without knowing it, Cleopas names the day Jesus had spoken of (9:22; 24:7).

decisions.choice: rescue Israel and set our people free
decisions.reason: Readable explains "redeem" in two plain phrases.

decisions.choice: it has been three days
decisions.reason: Readable counts the days in the everyday way; the sense is the same.

source.text: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

records.literal_gloss: But also women certain from us astonished us, having been early at the tomb \v 23 and not having found the body of him they came saying also a vision of angels to have seen, who say him to be alive.

en.L: But also some women from among us astonished us; they were at the tomb early, \v 23 and not finding {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who say that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is alive.
en.B: And then some women of our company gave us a shock. They went to the tomb at first light \v 23 and found that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body was gone. They came back and said they had even seen angels in a vision, angels who say that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is alive.
en.R: Then some of the women in our group surprised us. Early this morning they went to the tomb, \v 23 but {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body was not there. They came back and told us they had seen angels in a vision. The angels said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is alive!

fr.L: Mais aussi quelques femmes d’entre nous nous ont stupéfiés : elles ont été au tombeau de grand matin \v 23 et, n’ayant pas trouvé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps, elles sont venues dire qu’elles avaient même vu une vision d’anges, qui disent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vivant.
fr.B: Et puis quelques femmes de notre groupe nous ont bouleversés. Elles sont allées au tombeau dès l’aube \v 23 et n’ont pas trouvé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps. Elles sont revenues nous dire qu’elles avaient même vu des anges dans une vision, des anges qui disent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vivant.
fr.R: Ensuite, quelques femmes de notre groupe nous ont surpris. Tôt ce matin, elles sont allées au tombeau, \v 23 mais {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps n’était pas là. Elles sont revenues et nous ont dit qu’elles avaient vu des anges dans une vision. Les anges ont dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vivant !

decisions.choice: astonished us: threw us into confusion
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone out of their usual state of mind. The women's news amazed the disciples but did not convince them (24:11).

decisions.choice: a vision of angels: angels whom they saw
decisions.reason: The word is used for a real sight given by God, as when Zechariah saw an angel in the sanctuary (1:22). Luke has told of the two men in shining clothing (24:4).

decisions.choice: who say that he is alive: the angels' message reported in the present
alternatives: who said that he was alive
decisions.reason: Cleopas reports the message as something that still stands: he is alive.

decisions.choice: Early this morning
decisions.reason: Readable says which morning: the women went that same day (24:1).

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον, αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.

records.literal_gloss: And went some of those with us to the tomb, and found [it] so as also the women said, him however not they saw.

en.L: And some of those with us went off to the tomb and found [it] just as the women also had said, but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they did not see."
en.B: Some of our people went to the tomb as well. They found everything the way the women had described it, but they saw nothing of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Some of our friends went to the tomb too. Everything was the way the women said. But nobody saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Et quelques-uns de ceux [qui étaient] avec nous sont allés au tombeau et ont trouvé [les choses] comme les femmes aussi l’avaient dit, mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas vu. »
fr.B: Quelques-uns des nôtres sont allés eux aussi au tombeau. Ils ont tout trouvé comme les femmes l’avaient décrit, mais ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont vu nulle part. »
fr.R: Quelques-uns de nos amis sont allés au tombeau, eux aussi. Tout était comme les femmes l’avaient dit. Mais personne ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a vu. »

decisions.choice: some of those with us: Peter, and perhaps others
decisions.reason: Luke has told of Peter going to the tomb (24:12); John 20:3-10 tells of Peter and another disciple. The plural "some" leaves room for more than one.

decisions.choice: but him they did not see: the word "him" stands first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The tomb was empty, just as the women said, but no one had seen Jesus. The man they are speaking to is the one they did not see.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται·

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, O foolish [ones] and slow of heart to believe in all which spoke the prophets;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You are without understanding, and your hearts are slow to believe all that the prophets said!
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "You do not understand at all. Your hearts find it hard to believe everything the prophets said.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Ô insensés, et lents de cœur à croire tout ce qu’ont dit les prophètes !
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Vous ne comprenez donc pas ! Que votre cœur est lent à croire tout ce qu’ont dit les prophètes !
fr.R: Alors Jésus leur a dit : « Vous ne comprenez vraiment rien. Votre cœur a du mal à croire tout ce que les prophètes ont dit.

decisions.choice: foolish: without understanding
decisions.reason: The word means not using the mind, failing to see what is plain. Paul uses it of the Galatians (Galatians 3:1). It is a rebuke, not an insult.

decisions.choice: slow of heart: slow to take it in and trust it
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is where a person thinks and decides, not only feels.

decisions.choice: all that the prophets have spoken: the whole message, not only part of it
alternatives: some of what the prophets said
decisions.reason: They believed the promises of a king who would set Israel free (24:21) but not the words about his suffering.

decisions.choice: Ô insensés (L), with no noun; Vous ne comprenez donc pas (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is an adjective used as a noun (m1). French "Ô hommes sans intelligence" would add "men", and the second traveller is not named; the plural adjective alone is good French and keeps the Greek. Balanced and Readable turn the rebuke into a statement, as the English does.

source.text: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: Not these things was it necessary to suffer the Christ and to enter into the glory of him?

en.L: Was it not necessary for the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to suffer these things and to enter into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory?"
en.B: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} had to suffer these things and enter into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?"
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} had to suffer these things and then go into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory. Is that not true?"

fr.L: Ne fallait-il pas que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} souffre ces choses et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entre dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire ? »
fr.B: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} devait souffrir tout cela et entrer dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, n’est-ce pas ? »
fr.R: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} devait souffrir tout cela, puis entrer dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire. N’est-ce pas vrai ? »

decisions.choice: was it necessary: it had to be, by God's purpose
alternatives: it just turned out that way
decisions.reason: The same word as in 9:22, 24:7 and 24:44. The question expects the answer yes: the Scriptures show that the Christ had to suffer.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed King
decisions.reason: With the article it is a title, as in 9:20. The two hoped for a king who would redeem Israel (24:21); Jesus shows that the King had to suffer first.

decisions.choice: enter into his glory: be raised and exalted to God's right hand
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke of the Son of Man coming "in his glory" (9:26). Peter says that God raised Jesus and exalted him (Acts 2:32-36), and 1 Peter 1:11 speaks of the sufferings of Christ and the glories that follow.

decisions.choice: a statement followed by a question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the point and then ask for agreement, which is the force of the Greek question.

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Readable makes the order of events plain: suffering, then glory.

source.text: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having begun from Moses and from all the prophets he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

en.L: And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.B: Then, starting with Moses and going on through all the prophets, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} explained to them what was written about {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in every part of the Scriptures.
en.R: Then Jesus explained to them what the Scriptures said about {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. He started with the books of Moses and went on through all the books of the prophets.

fr.L: Et, commençant par Moïse et par tous les prophètes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur interpréta dans toutes les Écritures ce qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} concernait.
fr.B: Puis, commençant par Moïse et parcourant tous les prophètes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur expliqua ce qui était écrit à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet dans toutes les Écritures.
fr.R: Alors Jésus leur a expliqué ce que les Écritures disaient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il a commencé par les livres de Moïse et a continué avec tous les livres des prophètes.

decisions.choice: Moses and all the prophets: the Scriptures of Israel
alternatives: Moses and the prophets as people
decisions.reason: "Moses" means the five books of the law, which he was held to have written; "the prophets" are the books of the prophets (16:29, 31). Together they stand for the whole of Scripture.

decisions.choice: interpreted: explained the meaning
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to translate from another language (Acts 9:36), but here it means to explain.

decisions.choice: in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself: the Scriptures point to him
alternatives: only a few passages about the Messiah
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say only that a few verses speak of him. He shows how the whole of Scripture leads to his suffering and glory (24:44; John 5:39; Acts 3:18, 24).

decisions.choice: going on through (B); went on through (R)
decisions.reason: "Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets" means starting at the beginning and covering the whole; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and he made as if farther to be going.

en.L: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} acted as though {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were going farther.
en.B: They came near the village they were heading for, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the impression of going on farther.
en.R: When they came close to the village where they were going, Jesus acted as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going to keep walking.

fr.L: Et ils approchèrent du village où ils allaient, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit semblant d’aller plus loin.
fr.B: Ils approchèrent du village où ils se rendaient, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit mine d’aller plus loin.
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés près du village où ils allaient, Jésus a fait comme s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait continuer à marcher.

decisions.choice: acted as though he were going farther: gave them the choice to invite him in
decisions.reason: A traveler did not invite himself into a home; he waited to be asked. The angels at Sodom did the same until Lot pressed them to stay (Genesis 19:2-3). Jesus leaves the two free to ask him in.

source.text: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα.

records.literal_gloss: And they urged him saying, Stay with us, for toward evening it is and has declined already the day.

en.L: And they urged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Stay with us, because it is toward evening, and the day has already declined."
en.B: But they would not let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go on. "Stay with us," they said. "Evening is coming, and the daylight is already fading."
en.R: But they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Stay with us. It will soon be dark. The sun is already going down."

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pressèrent, disant : « Reste avec nous, car on est vers le soir et le jour est déjà sur son déclin. »
fr.B: Mais ils ne voulurent pas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laisser partir. « Reste avec nous, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent-ils. Le soir vient, et le jour baisse déjà. »
fr.R: Mais ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont supplié : « Reste avec nous. Il va bientôt faire nuit. Le soleil se couche déjà. »

decisions.choice: urged: pressed him strongly
decisions.reason: The verb is used of pressing an invitation until it is accepted, as Lydia pressed Paul and his companions to stay at her house (Acts 16:15).

decisions.choice: the day has already declined: the day is nearly over
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend or lean; the day is leaning toward evening, as in 9:12.

decisions.choice: they would not let him go on
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the strength of the verb.

source.text: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And he went in to stay with them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went in to stay with them.
en.B: He went inside to stay with them.
en.R: So Jesus went into the house to stay with them.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra pour rester avec eux.
fr.B: Il entra pour rester avec eux.
fr.R: Alors Jésus est entré dans la maison pour rester avec eux.

decisions.choice: into the house
decisions.reason: Readable says where he went in; it was a house in the village, perhaps the home of one of the two.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the reclining of him with them, having taken the bread he blessed [it], and having broken [it] he was giving [it] to them;

en.L: And it happened, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table] with them, taking the bread, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed [it], and breaking [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to give [it] to them.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the bread and said the blessing. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke it and handed it to them.
en.R: When Jesus sat down to eat with them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the bread and thanked God for it. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke it and gave it to them.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était mis à table avec eux, que, prenant le pain, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit la bénédiction, et, l’ayant rompu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à le leur donner.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut pris place à table avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit le pain et prononça la bénédiction. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le rompit et le leur donna.
fr.R: Quand Jésus s’est mis à table avec eux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a pris le pain et a remercié Dieu. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a rompu et le leur a donné.

decisions.choice: reclined: took his place for the meal
decisions.reason: People reclined on cushions or couches at a meal, leaning on one elbow (7:36).

decisions.choice: he blessed it: he spoke the blessing that praised God for the bread
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing of God over the bread. It was the host's part to say it; the guest has taken the host's place.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the words of the feeding and of the Last Supper
alternatives: an ordinary meal described in ordinary words
decisions.reason: The same actions are described when Jesus fed the five thousand (9:16) and at the Last Supper (22:19). The two recognize him as he does them (24:35).

decisions.choice: began to give: the imperfect tense
decisions.reason: The past continuous tense pictures him in the act of handing out the bread, at the moment their eyes are opened.

decisions.choice: thanked God for it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the blessing as praise and thanks to God, as at 9:16.

source.text: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Of them then were opened the eyes and they recognized him; and he invisible became from them.

en.L: And their eyes were opened, and they recognized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became invisible to them.
en.B: Then their eyes were opened and they knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could no longer be seen.
en.R: Then their eyes were opened, and they knew it was Jesus. At that moment {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} disappeared.

fr.L: Alors leurs yeux furent ouverts et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devint invisible pour eux.
fr.B: Alors leurs yeux furent ouverts et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} cessa d’être visible pour eux.
fr.R: Alors leurs yeux ont été ouverts, et ils ont reconnu que c’était Jésus. Au même moment, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a disparu.

decisions.choice: were opened: the passive, as in 24:16
decisions.reason: Their eyes were held back on the road (24:16) and are now opened. Luke uses the same verb for Jesus opening the Scriptures (24:32) and their minds (24:45).

decisions.choice: became invisible: he was no longer seen
decisions.reason: The word means unseen. The risen Jesus comes and goes in ways an ordinary body cannot (24:36).

decisions.choice: they knew it was Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly whom they recognized.

source.text: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν ὡς ἐλάλει ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς;

records.literal_gloss: And they said to one another, Not the heart of us burning was within us as he was speaking to us on the road, as he was opening to us the Scriptures?

en.L: And they said to one another, "Was not our heart burning within us as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking to us on the road, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was opening the Scriptures to us?"
en.B: They said to each other, "Did we not feel our hearts on fire inside us while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} talked with us on the road and laid the Scriptures open to us?"
en.R: They said to each other, "While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking with us on the road and explaining the Scriptures, did we not feel something like a fire in our hearts?"

fr.L: Et ils se dirent l’un à l’autre : « Notre cœur n’était-il pas brûlant en nous, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous parlait sur le chemin, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous ouvrait les Écritures ? »
fr.B: Ils se dirent l’un à l’autre : « N’avons-nous pas senti notre cœur s’enflammer en nous, pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous parlait en chemin et nous ouvrait le sens des Écritures ? »
fr.R: Ils se sont dit : « Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous parlait sur la route et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous expliquait les Écritures, est-ce qu’on ne sentait pas comme un feu dans notre cœur ? »

decisions.choice: our heart was burning within us: we were deeply stirred
decisions.reason: A burning heart is a picture of strong feeling stirred by God's word. Jeremiah says God's word was like a fire shut up in his bones (Jeremiah 20:9).

decisions.choice: within us: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them P75 and Codex Vaticanus, lack "within us"; most others have it. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: opening the Scriptures: explaining their meaning
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for their eyes being opened (24:31). Jesus opened the Scriptures to them, then opened their eyes.

decisions.choice: the time clause first, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable puts the setting first so the question is short.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστάντες αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ εὗρον ἠθροισμένους τοὺς ἕνδεκα καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς, λέγοντας ὅτι ὄντως ἠγέρθη ὁ κύριος καὶ ὤφθη Σίμωνι.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen up in that same hour they returned to Jerusalem, and found gathered together the eleven and those with them, \v 34 saying that indeed has been raised the Lord and has appeared to Simon.

en.L: And getting up that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven gathered together, and those with them, \v 34 saying, "The Lord has really been raised, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appeared to Simon!"
en.B: Without delay they got up and went back to Jerusalem. They found the Eleven gathered with their companions, \v 34 who were saying, "The Lord has truly been raised, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appeared to Simon!"
en.R: Right away they got up and went back to Jerusalem. There they found the eleven apostles and the others who were with them. \v 34 They were saying, "The Lord really has risen from death! He has appeared to Simon!"

fr.L: Et, se levant à l’heure même, ils retournèrent à Jérusalem, et ils trouvèrent rassemblés les onze et ceux [qui étaient] avec eux, \v 34 disant : « Le Seigneur a vraiment été ressuscité, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est apparu à Simon ! »
fr.B: Sans attendre, ils se levèrent et retournèrent à Jérusalem. Ils y trouvèrent les Onze réunis avec leurs compagnons, \v 34 qui disaient : « Le Seigneur a vraiment été ressuscité, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est apparu à Simon ! »
fr.R: Tout de suite, ils se sont levés et sont retournés à Jérusalem. Là, ils ont trouvé les onze apôtres et les autres qui étaient avec eux. \v 34 Ceux-ci disaient : « Le Seigneur est vraiment ressuscité ! Il est apparu à Simon ! »

decisions.choice: that same hour: at once
decisions.reason: "Hour" is often used for a moment or a short time. Though it was evening (24:29), they set out at once for Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: saying: the eleven and their companions are the ones speaking
alternatives: the two from Emmaus are speaking
decisions.reason: The word "saying" agrees with "the eleven and those with them". Before the two can tell their news, the others greet them with theirs.

decisions.choice: Simon: Simon Peter
decisions.reason: Luke calls Peter Simon (5:3-10; 22:31). His meeting with the risen Lord is not told, but Paul names Cephas, which is Peter, as the first of the apostles to see him (1 Corinthians 15:5).

decisions.choice: has appeared: has been seen
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the appearances of the risen Jesus (Acts 13:31; 1 Corinthians 15:5-8). It means a real meeting.

decisions.choice: has really been raised: God has raised him
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, as in 24:6. "Really" answers the doubt of the morning (24:11).

decisions.choice: Without delay (B); Right away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the time phrase.

decisions.choice: has risen from death
decisions.reason: Readable uses the active verb, which children understand more easily; Jesus also speaks of himself as rising (24:7, 46).

source.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξηγοῦντο τὰ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καὶ ὡς ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου.

records.literal_gloss: And they were relating the things on the road and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.

en.L: And they told the things [that happened] on the road, and how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
en.B: The two then told their own story: what took place on the road, and how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became known to them in the breaking of the bread.
en.R: Then the two followers told what had happened to them on the road. They told how they knew it was Jesus when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the bread.

fr.L: Et eux racontaient ce qui [s’était passé] sur le chemin, et comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était fait reconnaître d’eux à la fraction du pain.
fr.B: Les deux racontèrent à leur tour ce qui s’était passé en chemin, et comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était fait reconnaître d’eux au moment de rompre le pain.
fr.R: Alors les deux disciples ont raconté ce qui leur était arrivé sur la route. Ils ont raconté comment ils avaient reconnu Jésus quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait rompu le pain.

decisions.choice: they: the two, now telling their side
decisions.reason: The pronoun is emphatic: after the others have told about Simon, the two tell what happened to them.

decisions.choice: the breaking of the bread: the meal he shared with them
decisions.reason: Breaking the bread began a Jewish meal. Luke uses the same phrase for the shared meals of the first believers (Acts 2:42), where Jesus' followers met him again in the meal.

decisions.choice: was made known: the passive
decisions.reason: The two did not figure it out; it was shown to them (24:31).

decisions.choice: the two (B); the two followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which group is speaking.

source.text: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: These things now them speaking, he himself stood in [the] midst of them.

en.L: And while they were saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} stood in [the] middle of them.
en.B: As they were talking about all this, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was standing among them.
en.R: While they were talking about this, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} suddenly stood among them.

fr.L: Et tandis qu’ils disaient ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} se tint au milieu d’eux.
fr.B: Ils parlaient encore de tout cela quand Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} se tint là, au milieu d’eux.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils parlaient de tout cela, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} s’est soudain trouvé debout au milieu d’eux.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with "among them", as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sentence goes on, "and he says to them, Peace to you", the reading of most manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, add "and he says to them, Peace to you". Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack the words, and the SBLGNT follows them here. The same words are found in John 20:19, and some think they came from there. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he himself stood among them: Jesus appears without coming through a door
decisions.reason: Luke does not say how he came; he had vanished at Emmaus in the same way (24:31). "Himself" stresses that it was Jesus in person.

decisions.choice: suddenly
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the surprise of his coming, which 24:37 shows.

source.text: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Having been startled however and terrified having become they were thinking a spirit to see.

en.L: But being startled and becoming terrified, they thought they were seeing a spirit.
en.B: But they were alarmed and filled with fear, for they thought they were looking at a spirit.
en.R: They were shocked and very much afraid. They thought a ghost was standing there.

fr.L: Mais, effrayés et devenus pleins de crainte, ils pensaient voir un esprit.
fr.B: Mais ils furent saisis d’effroi et de crainte, car ils croyaient voir un esprit.
fr.R: Ils ont eu un choc et ils ont eu très peur. Ils pensaient qu’ils voyaient un fantôme.

decisions.choice: a spirit: a ghost, someone dead seen without a body
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for spirit. Here it means the spirit of a dead person seen by the living, as Jesus' answer shows: a spirit has no flesh and bones (24:39).

decisions.choice: startled and terrified: fear that grows
decisions.reason: Two words are joined to show how great their fear was.

decisions.choice: a ghost
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for what they thought they saw; Literal and Balanced keep "spirit" to match Jesus' words in 24:39.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Why troubled are you, and for what reason doubts come up in the heart of you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you troubled, and for what reason do doubts rise up in your heart?
en.B: He said to them, "Why are you so shaken? Why are these doubts coming up in your hearts?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Why are you so upset? Why do you have doubts in your hearts?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Pourquoi êtes-vous troublés, et pourquoi des doutes montent-ils dans votre cœur ?
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Pourquoi êtes-vous si bouleversés ? Pourquoi ces doutes surgissent-ils dans vos cœurs ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Pourquoi êtes-vous si inquiets ? Pourquoi avez-vous des doutes dans vos cœurs ?

decisions.choice: doubts: questioning thoughts
decisions.reason: The word is used for inner reasoning, often for thoughts that question or resist (2:35; 5:22). They cannot believe what they see.

decisions.choice: your heart: singular, the heart of the group
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the singular for something each person in a group has.

decisions.choice: hearts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the heart of each person present.

source.text: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός· ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.

records.literal_gloss: See the hands of me and the feet of me, that I am he myself; touch me and see, because a spirit flesh and bones not has as me you see having.

en.L: See {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet, that it is I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}; touch {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have."
en.B: Look at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet, and see that it is really I. Feel {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and see. Spirits have no flesh and bones; you can see that I do."
en.R: Look at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet! It is really {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Touch {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and see. A ghost does not have a body of flesh and bones, but you can see that I do."

fr.L: Voyez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} pieds : c’est bien {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} ; touchez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et voyez, car un esprit n’a ni chair ni os, comme vous voyez que j’en ai. »
fr.B: Regardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} pieds : c’est bien {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Palpez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et voyez. Un esprit n’a ni chair ni os, et vous voyez que j’en ai. »
fr.R: Regardez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} pieds ! C’est vraiment {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ! Touchez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et voyez. Un fantôme n’a pas un corps de chair et d’os, mais vous voyez que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, j’en ai un. »

decisions.choice: my hands and my feet: the marks that show who he is
alternatives: his hands and feet as proof of a body only
decisions.reason: The hands and feet had been nailed to the cross. John tells that Jesus showed the marks of the nails (John 20:20, 25-27). Luke does not mention the wounds, but the hands and feet show that this is the same Jesus who was crucified.

decisions.choice: it is I myself: the same person, not another
decisions.reason: The words stress identity: the one they see is the very one they knew.

decisions.choice: touch: handle, feel with the hands
decisions.reason: The verb is used for feeling something to find out what it is. 1 John 1:1 speaks of what "our hands have touched".

decisions.choice: flesh and bones: the risen Jesus has a real body
alternatives: a body that only looks real
decisions.reason: Jesus is not a ghost or a vision. He has been raised in the body that was buried, and he can be touched and can eat (24:42-43; Acts 1:3; 10:41).

decisions.choice: Feel me
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out that they are to handle him to find out that he is solid.

decisions.choice: a ghost
decisions.reason: Readable uses "ghost", as in 24:37.

source.text: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.

records.literal_gloss: And this having said he showed to them the hands and the feet.

en.L: And having said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed them [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands and feet.
en.B: After saying this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and feet.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

fr.L: Et, ayant dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur montra les mains et les pieds.
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur fit voir {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds.
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a montré {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds.

decisions.choice: the verse is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin and Syriac manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have the verse. Codex Bezae, some Old Latin manuscripts and some early Syriac manuscripts lack it. Some think it was added from John 20:20, where Jesus shows his hands and side; but Luke has hands and feet, as in 24:39. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: les mains et les pieds (L), with no bracketed possessive
alternatives: [ses] mains et [ses] pieds, as the English Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article only. French, like Greek, uses the article for parts of the body when the owner is plain, so Literal can follow it without supplying "his"; Balanced and Readable say "ses", with the pronoun setting.

source.text: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;

records.literal_gloss: Still now disbelieving them for the joy and marveling he said to them, Have you anything to eat here?

en.L: And while they were still not believing for joy, and were marveling, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Do you have anything to eat here?"
en.B: Their joy and amazement were so great that they still could not believe it. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Do you have something here to eat?"
en.R: They were so full of joy and amazement that they still could not believe it was true. Jesus asked them, "Do you have any food here?"

fr.L: Et comme ils ne croyaient pas encore, de joie, et s’étonnaient, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Avez-vous ici quelque chose à manger ? »
fr.B: Leur joie et leur étonnement étaient si grands qu’ils n’arrivaient pas encore à croire. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « Avez-vous ici de quoi manger ? »
