fr.R: Ils étaient si pleins de joie et si étonnés qu’ils n’arrivaient toujours pas à croire que c’était vrai. Jésus leur a demandé : « Est-ce que vous avez quelque chose à manger ici ? »

decisions.choice: not believing for joy: it seemed too good to be true
decisions.reason: Their doubt now comes from joy, not from fear. Luke says the same of Rhoda, who was so glad to hear Peter that she did not open the door (Acts 12:14).

decisions.choice: Do you have anything to eat: food to show that he has a real body
decisions.reason: Eating in front of them gives them another sign that he is not a spirit. Peter later says that the apostles ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead (Acts 10:41).

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the result
alternatives: while they were still not believing for joy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out that their joy kept them from believing.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος·

records.literal_gloss: They and gave to him of a fish broiled a piece;

en.L: And they gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a piece of a broiled fish.
en.B: They handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a piece of grilled fish.
en.R: They gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a piece of cooked fish.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnèrent un morceau de poisson grillé.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} présentèrent un morceau de poisson grillé.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont donné un morceau de poisson cuit.

decisions.choice: a piece of broiled fish: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a piece of broiled fish and some honeycomb, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and some honeycomb". The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: broiled: cooked over a fire
decisions.reason: Fish from the Lake of Galilee was a common food, often cooked over coals (John 21:9).

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken [it] before them he ate.

en.L: And taking [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ate [it] before them.
en.B: He took it and ate it while they watched.
en.R: Jesus took it and ate it while they watched.

fr.L: Et, l’ayant pris, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mangea devant eux.
fr.B: Il le prit et le mangea sous leurs yeux.
fr.R: Jésus l’a pris et l’a mangé pendant qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} regardaient.

decisions.choice: before them: in front of them, as witnesses
decisions.reason: Luke stresses that they saw him eat. They are to be witnesses (24:48).

source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι μου οὓς ἐλάλησα πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔτι ὢν σὺν ὑμῖν, ὅτι δεῖ πληρωθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσέως καὶ προφήταις καὶ ψαλμοῖς περὶ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them, These [are] the words of me which I spoke to you still being with you, that it is necessary to be fulfilled all things having been written in the law of Moses and Prophets and Psalms concerning me.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "These [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all the things written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms must be fulfilled."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This is what I was telling you when I was still with you: whatever the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms have written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must be fulfilled."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "This is what I was telling you when I was with you before. Everything written about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the Law of Moses, in the books of the prophets, and in the Psalms must come true."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Ce [sont] là {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, que je vous ai dites quand j’étais encore avec vous : il faut que s’accomplisse tout ce qui est écrit à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet dans la Loi de Moïse, et les Prophètes, et les Psaumes. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Voilà ce que je vous disais quand j’étais encore avec vous : tout ce que la Loi de Moïse, les Prophètes et les Psaumes ont écrit à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet doit s’accomplir. »
fr.R: Puis Jésus leur a dit : « C’est ce que je vous disais quand j’étais avec vous auparavant. Tout ce qui est écrit sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} dans la Loi de Moïse, dans les livres des prophètes et dans les Psaumes doit se réaliser. »

decisions.choice: while I was still with you: before his death
alternatives: while he was still on earth
decisions.reason: Jesus is with them now, but not as he was before. His time of living and traveling with them came to an end at the cross.

decisions.choice: the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms: the whole of the Hebrew Scriptures
decisions.reason: The Hebrew Scriptures were grouped as the Law, the Prophets and the Writings. The Psalms were the largest and best known of the Writings, and the name could stand for the whole group. Jesus names every part of Scripture.

decisions.choice: must be fulfilled: by God's purpose
decisions.reason: The same word of necessity as in 24:7 and 24:26. What God has said in Scripture has to come to pass.

decisions.choice: these are my words: the warnings he gave about his suffering and rising
decisions.reason: Jesus refers to what he said many times (9:22, 9:44; 18:31-33; 22:37).

decisions.choice: come true
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for being fulfilled.

decisions.choice: the books of the prophets
decisions.reason: Readable says that the Prophets are part of the Scriptures.

source.text: τότε διήνοιξεν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι οὕτως γέγραπται παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ·

records.literal_gloss: Then he opened of them the mind to understand the Scriptures, \v 46 and he said to them that thus it has been written to suffer the Christ and to rise out from [the] dead the third day, \v 47 and to be proclaimed in the name of him repentance and forgiveness of sins to all the nations, having begun from Jerusalem;

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened their mind to understand the Scriptures, \v 46 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Thus it is written, that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is to suffer and to rise from [the] dead on the third day, \v 47 and that repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened their minds to make sense of the Scriptures. \v 46 He told them, "This is what stands written: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, \v 47 and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name repentance and the forgiveness of sins are to be announced to all the nations, starting from Jerusalem.
en.R: Then Jesus helped them understand the Scriptures. \v 46 He said to them, "This is what the Scriptures say: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} would suffer and then rise from the dead on the third day. \v 47 And in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, people of every nation will be told to turn away from their sins and be forgiven. This will begin in Jerusalem.

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ouvrit l’intelligence pour comprendre les Écritures, \v 46 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Ainsi il est écrit que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} doit souffrir et ressusciter d’entre les morts le troisième jour, \v 47 et que la repentance et le pardon des péchés doivent être proclamés en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom à toutes les nations, à commencer par Jérusalem.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ouvrit l’esprit pour qu’ils comprennent les Écritures. \v 46 Il leur dit : « Voici ce qui est écrit : le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} doit souffrir et ressusciter d’entre les morts le troisième jour, \v 47 et en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom la repentance et le pardon des péchés doivent être annoncés à toutes les nations, en commençant par Jérusalem.
fr.R: Alors Jésus les a aidés à comprendre les Écritures. \v 46 Il leur a dit : « Voici ce que disent les Écritures : le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} allait souffrir, puis revenir à la vie le troisième jour. \v 47 Et en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, on va dire aux gens de tous les peuples de se détourner de leurs péchés pour être pardonnés. Cela va commencer à Jérusalem.

decisions.choice: opened their mind: gave them understanding
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for their eyes (24:31) and for the Scriptures (24:32). Understanding Scripture is given by the risen Lord, not only learned.

decisions.choice: thus it is written: the Scriptures as a whole, not one verse
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a passage. In Acts the apostles point to passages such as Psalm 16 for his rising (Acts 2:25-31) and Isaiah 53 for his suffering (Acts 8:32-35).

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed King
decisions.reason: With the article it is a title, as in 24:26.

decisions.choice: repentance and forgiveness of sins: turning back to God and being freed from sins
alternatives: a change of mind about Jesus only
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of mind and life, a turning back to God (3:3, 8; 5:32). Forgiveness is a release from sins, as Zechariah foretold (1:77) and Jesus announced (4:18). The apostles preach both in Acts 2:38.

decisions.choice: repentance and forgiveness: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: repentance for the forgiveness of sins, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "and". Some early ones, among them P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "for": repentance that leads to forgiveness, as in 3:3. The meaning is close. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: all the nations: all peoples, the Gentiles included
alternatives: the Jewish people scattered among the nations
decisions.reason: Simeon said Jesus would be a light for revelation to the Gentiles (2:32). Acts tells how the message went from Jerusalem to the nations (Acts 1:8).

decisions.choice: beginning from Jerusalem: the starting point of the preaching
alternatives: the start of the next sentence: "Beginning from Jerusalem, you are witnesses"
decisions.reason: The word "beginning" is plural and could go with the witnesses in 24:48. The SBLGNT punctuation joins it to this sentence, where it says where the preaching starts.

decisions.choice: rise from the dead: come back to life
decisions.reason: The verb is active here, as in 18:33 and 24:7.

decisions.choice: This is what stands written (B); This is what the Scriptures say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the formula a full sentence and introduce what follows with a colon.

decisions.choice: will be told to turn away from their sins and be forgiven
alternatives: repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed
decisions.reason: Readable turns the nouns into verbs, which are easier to follow.

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Readable makes the order of events plain, as at 24:26.

source.text: ὑμεῖς ἐστε μάρτυρες τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: You [are] witnesses of these things.

en.L: You are witnesses of these things.
en.B: You are witnesses to these things.
en.R: You have seen all these things, and you are to tell others about them.

fr.L: Vous, vous êtes témoins de ces choses.
fr.B: C’est vous qui êtes les témoins de tout cela.
fr.R: Vous avez vu tout cela, et vous devez le raconter aux autres.

decisions.choice: witnesses: those who saw and will tell
decisions.reason: A witness is one who has seen something and speaks about it. In Acts the apostles are witnesses of the risen Jesus (Acts 1:8, 22; 2:32). The later sense, one who dies for the faith, grew out of this word.

decisions.choice: you: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stated and stands first: the people in that room are the ones who will carry the message.

decisions.choice: You have seen all these things, and you are to tell others about them.
alternatives: You are witnesses of these things.
decisions.reason: Readable explains both parts of being a witness: seeing and telling.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐξαποστέλλω τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρός μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς· ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν.

records.literal_gloss: And behold I am sending the promise of the Father of me upon you; you however stay in the city until you are clothed from on high [with] power.

en.L: And look, I am sending the promise of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father upon you; but you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
en.B: I am sending upon you what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father promised. As for you, remain here in the city until power from on high clothes you."
en.R: I am going to send you the Holy Spirit, whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father promised. But stay here in the city until you receive power from heaven."

fr.L: Et voici, moi, j’envoie sur vous la promesse de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père ; mais vous, restez dans la ville jusqu’à ce que vous soyez revêtus de puissance d’en haut. »
fr.B: J’envoie sur vous ce que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père a promis. Quant à vous, restez ici dans la ville jusqu’à ce que la puissance d’en haut vous revête. »
fr.R: Je vais vous envoyer l’Esprit Saint, que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père a promis. Mais restez ici, dans la ville, jusqu’à ce que vous receviez la puissance qui vient du ciel. »

decisions.choice: the promise of my Father: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: In Acts Jesus tells the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for what the Father promised, and says they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:4-5, 8). Peter says Jesus received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and poured him out (Acts 2:33). John the Baptist had foretold it (3:16).

decisions.choice: I am sending: a present that points to what is about to happen
decisions.reason: The present tense describes something certain and near. The Spirit came at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: clothed with power: power put on like clothing
decisions.reason: The Hebrew Scriptures say the Spirit of the LORD "clothed" Gideon (Judges 6:34). "From on high" means from God in heaven (1:78; Isaiah 32:15).

decisions.choice: the city: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the city of Jerusalem, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "of Jerusalem". The earliest lack it. The city is Jerusalem either way (24:47, 52). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this word to draw attention to his promise. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit, whom my Father promised
decisions.reason: Readable names the promise, as Acts 1:4-5 and 2:33 do.

decisions.choice: receive power from heaven
alternatives: are clothed with power from on high
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of clothing and the phrase "from on high".

source.text: Ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἕως πρὸς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ἐπάρας τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: He led out then them as far as to Bethany, and having lifted up the hands of him he blessed them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them out as far as toward Bethany, and lifting up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blessed them.
en.B: He led them out until they were near Bethany. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and blessed them.
en.R: Then Jesus led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers out of the city to a place near the village of Bethany. He lifted up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and blessed them.

fr.L: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les emmena dehors jusque vers Béthanie, et, levant {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les bénit.
fr.B: Il les emmena dehors, jusque près de Béthanie. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leva {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains et les bénit.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a emmené {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples hors de la ville, jusqu’à un endroit près du village de Béthanie. Il a levé les mains et les a bénis.

decisions.choice: as far as toward Bethany: to the area near Bethany
decisions.reason: Bethany was a village on the far side of the Mount of Olives, about two miles from Jerusalem (19:29). Acts 1:12 says they returned from the Mount of Olives.

decisions.choice: lifting up his hands, he blessed them: as a priest blesses the people
decisions.reason: Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them (Leviticus 9:22). The Gospel began with a priest, Zechariah, who came out of the sanctuary unable to speak to the waiting people (1:21-22); it ends with Jesus blessing his people.

decisions.choice: when this happened: Luke does not mark the time
alternatives: the same day as the resurrection
decisions.reason: Read alone, the Gospel seems to tell the events of 24:36-53 on one day. Luke's second book says Jesus appeared to the apostles over forty days before he was taken up (Acts 1:3).

decisions.choice: his followers out of the city
decisions.reason: Readable says who went and where they went from.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the blessing of him them, he parted from them and was being carried up into the heaven.

en.L: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was blessing them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
en.B: He was still blessing them when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} parted from them and was borne up into heaven.
en.R: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was blessing them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away from them. God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up into heaven.

fr.L: Et il arriva, tandis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les bénissait, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se sépara d’eux et fut emporté au ciel.
fr.B: Il les bénissait encore quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se sépara d’eux et fut enlevé au ciel.
fr.R: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les bénissait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a quittés. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a emporté au ciel.

decisions.choice: and was carried up into heaven: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and in Codex Bezae
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have these words. The first copyist of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Bezae, with some Old Latin manuscripts, lack them. Luke says in Acts 1:2 that his first book went up to the day Jesus was taken up, which fits the longer text. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was carried up: God took him up
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: he was taken up. Acts 1:9-11 tells more, with a cloud that took him out of their sight.

decisions.choice: parted from them: went away from them
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand apart or to separate. With the following words it means he left them.

decisions.choice: God took him up
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who took him, as the passive implies (Acts 1:2, 11).

decisions.choice: having worshiped him: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have "having worshiped him". Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack it. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: worshiped him: bowed before Jesus as one bows before God
alternatives: honored him as a great man
decisions.reason: Jesus had told the devil that worship belongs to God alone (4:8). For the first time in Luke, his followers worship Jesus.

decisions.choice: with great joy: the joy the angel announced at his birth
decisions.reason: The angel brought the shepherds good news of great joy (2:10). The Gospel ends where it began, with joy and in the temple (1:8-9, 14).

decisions.choice: blessing God: praising and thanking God
decisions.reason: When people bless God they speak well of him, praising and thanking him, as Zechariah and Simeon did (1:64; 2:28).

decisions.choice: blessing God: the reading of the SBLGNT, with no "Amen"
alternatives: praising God, the reading of Codex Bezae
praising and blessing God, the reading of many manuscripts
Amen added at the end, as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts, among them P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "blessing". Codex Bezae reads "praising", and many later manuscripts join the two. Many later manuscripts also end the book with "Amen". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in the temple: in the courts of the temple at the times of prayer
decisions.reason: The temple courts were open to worshipers, and the first believers met there daily (Acts 2:46; 3:1).

decisions.choice: giving thanks and praise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what blessing God means.

decisions.choice: bowed down in worship before him
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out that the verb describes bowing low.

decisions.choice: l’ayant adoré (L); se prosternèrent devant lui pour l’adorer (B); l’ont adoré (R)
decisions.reason: The verb names bowing low before Jesus as one bows before God (m2). French "adorer" is the word for worship given to God, so every level uses it; Balanced also keeps the gesture, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: This word names the whole temple area, and the disciples met in its courts at the times of prayer (m6); only priests entered the sanctuary. As the style guide has it, Literal says "le temple" and Balanced and Readable say where they were.
